summary: Players draw, discard, and play cards to be the first to build a stable of seven unicorns, while everyone else uses Neigh and Downgrade cards to destroy, steal, or sabotage each other's progress. Games are short, chaotic, and heavy on direct player attacks, with little long-term planning since board states can be undone in a single turn.
praised: Cute, colorful unicorn art and irreverent humor land well with casual and younger players
Very easy to teach and quick to set up
Large card pool and expansions/themed decks add replayability and collectibility
Good gateway game for non-gamers or family game night
criticised: Shallow decision-making with little meaningful strategy once you know the cards
Take-that destruction can feel mean-spirited or frustrating, especially for younger or newer players who get repeatedly targeted
High luck/swinginess from the draw means a strong position can be erased instantly
Little appeal for hobbyist gamers looking for depth

interaction.kind: open conflict via direct attacks, stealing, and destroying opponents' cards

scoring.why: the winner is simply whoever completes a 7-unicorn stable first, with no separate scoring system
